name: Efficient Reasoning during Inference
description: Methods that improve reasoning efficiency at inference time by constraining the reasoning budget, allocating resources across different systems or models, and incorporating parallel search strategies.

items.name: Length Budgeting
items.description: Explicitly budgets computational resources during inference by managing the length of the reasoning chain. Includes prompt-based constraints, forced end-of-thinking delimiters, and difficulty-adaptive budget allocation.
items.hard_negative: Training the model with SFT or RL to produce shorter reasoning — length budgeting operates purely at inference time via prompts or decoding strategies.

items.name: System Switch
items.description: Dynamically alternates between fast intuitive reasoning (System 1) and slow deliberative reasoning (System 2) based on task complexity, drawing on dual process theory.
items.hard_negative: Routing queries to entirely different models of different sizes — system switch toggles reasoning modes within a single model or framework.

items.name: Model Switch
items.description: Allocates computational budgets across different models, such as routing queries between large and small models or using speculative decoding with draft models for verification.
items.hard_negative: Switching between System 1 and System 2 reasoning modes within one model — model switch involves distinct separate models.

items.name: Parallel Search
items.description: Generates multiple candidate outputs concurrently and employs early termination or pruning to reduce latency. Includes Best-of-N variants, tree-search, and combined sequential-parallel approaches.
items.hard_negative: Sequential revision where the model iteratively refines a single reasoning trace — parallel search generates and evaluates multiple candidates simultaneously.

name: Efficient Reasoning with SFT
description: Methods that fine-tune models via supervised learning to internalize concise reasoning, either by compressing explicit reasoning chains or by shifting reasoning into latent space representations.

items.name: Reasoning Chain Compression
items.description: Builds target datasets with concise reasoning paths or compresses existing reasoning chains to remove redundant information, then trains the model to internalize concise reasoning via supervised fine-tuning.
items.hard_negative: Replacing explicit CoT steps with continuous hidden representations — chain compression still produces explicit text tokens, just fewer of them.

items.name: Latent-Space SFT
items.description: Replaces explicit chain-of-thought steps with continuous hidden representations. Models reason in latent space using hidden states fed back as inputs, reducing token overhead while preserving reasoning capability.
items.hard_negative: Compressing explicit CoT text into shorter text sequences — latent-space SFT operates on continuous hidden representations, not discrete tokens.

name: Efficient Reasoning with RL
description: Methods that use reinforcement learning to optimize the trade-off between reasoning depth and token efficiency.

items.name: with Length Reward
items.description: Treats reasoning length as a trajectory-level resource, framing efficient reasoning as a constrained optimization problem where the objective is to remain within a soft or target budget while preserving correctness.
items.hard_negative: Step-level rewards that evaluate individual reasoning steps — trajectory-level methods operate on the entire reasoning trace as a unit.

items.name: without Length Reward
items.description: Improves reasoning efficiency without introducing direct length-related rewards, exploiting implicit biases from RL formulations, preference modeling, or training dynamics to let efficient reasoning emerge naturally.
phrases: preference optimization between concise and extended traces
items.hard_negative: Explicitly adding a length penalty term to the reward function — implicit methods achieve efficiency through algorithmic properties or preference modeling, not direct length rewards.

name: Efficient Reasoning during Pre-training
description: Pretraining approaches designed to accelerate reasoning efficiency through latent space pretraining, subquadratic attention mechanisms, and linearization of transformer models.

items.name: Latent-space Pretraining
items.description: Explores continuous representations instead of traditional token-based approaches during pretraining, enhancing depth of understanding and efficiency through dynamically sized patches, concept-level processing, or latent thought vectors.
items.hard_negative: Latent-space SFT where a pretrained model is fine-tuned to reason in hidden states — this category covers pretraining from scratch with latent representations.

items.name: Subquadratic Attention
items.description: Replaces standard self-attention in transformers with mechanisms that reduce the quadratic complexity of processing sequences, including linear sequence modeling and sparse attention.
items.hard_negative: Compressing the reasoning chain text to be shorter — subquadratic attention reduces the computational cost of processing any given sequence length.

items.name: Linearization
items.description: Converts pre-trained standard transformer models into linear recurrent structures, enhancing deployment efficiency without requiring extensive retraining from scratch.
items.hard_negative: Pretraining a linear model from scratch — linearization starts from a pretrained transformer and converts it into a more efficient architecture.

items.name: Efficient Reasoning with Subquadratic Attention
items.description: Studies that specifically explore efficient reasoning solutions using subquadratic attention models, investigating distillation, architectural modifications, and hybrid architectures for reasoning tasks.
items.hard_negative: General subquadratic attention architectures not specifically evaluated on reasoning tasks — this category focuses on applying these architectures to CoT reasoning.

name: Future Directions
description: Potential future research directions for efficient reasoning in the era of LRMs.

items.name: Efficient Multimodality and Video Reasoning
items.description: Focuses on dynamically adjusting the complexity of reasoning processes to align with the inherent difficulty of multimodal and video inputs, employing strategies like atomic step decomposition to handle noisy visual information.
phrases: Dynamic reasoning strategies across different modalities
items.hard_negative: Uniform reasoning processes regardless of input type — this category focuses on dynamically adjusting reasoning depth based on specific modalities and task complexities.

items.name: Efficient Test-time Scaling and Infinity Thinking
items.description: Investigates scaling compute dynamically during inference via search width (parallel sampling) and search depth (sequential revision), including transforming reasoning into iterative processes with intermediate summaries to achieve infinite thinking capabilities.
phrases: Balancing search depth with search width
items.hard_negative: Training-time computation scaling — this covers techniques that allocate compute on-the-fly during the test phase, including infinite reasoning loops.

items.name: Efficient and Trustworthy Reasoning
items.description: Addresses the safety and reliability challenges introduced by long reasoning chains, focusing on developing mechanisms to prevent models from exposing sensitive information during thought processes or accumulating noisy, untrustworthy information that leads to hallucinations.
phrases: Safe rate of the thinking process
items.hard_negative: Optimizing reasoning speed without regard to output safety or factual alignment — this area strictly targets the intersection of efficiency, safety, and hallucination mitigation.

items.name: Efficient Reasoning Applications
items.description: Applies efficient reasoning techniques to practical real-world systems, such as Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), autonomous agents, and tool learning, using strategies like dynamic knowledge retrieval and early exit mechanisms.
items.hard_negative: Core architectural or foundational model training — this focuses on the downstream application layer like agents, RAG, and tools.

items.name: Evaluation and Benchmark
items.description: Develops new metrics and datasets designed to quantify reasoning efficiency, overthinking phenomena, and the trade-offs between answer accuracy and computational token costs.
phrases: Trade-offs between accuracy and token consumption
items.hard_negative: Standard capability benchmarks that only measure final answer correctness — these benchmarks explicitly measure the cost, verbosity, and efficiency of the reasoning process itself.
